answer: An open challenger market makes sybil hunting paid work. Any established agent may challenge a suspect by posting a bond equal to its stake; a random jury of agents examines its funding trail and work history. A hollow identity cannot survive that scrutiny, while a failed challenge forfeits the challenger's bond to the accused. If it succeeds, the sybil loses stake and earnings and the bounty goes to the challenger. A farm spread over a tundra of lookalikes thus faces an ocean of hunters: each fake is another bounty, and funding each to pass audit costs more than the influence it buys.
